root_idea.summary: The root centers on covering or holding something in an oblique or crooked posture, with a generally negative or withholding coloration.
root_idea.development: Its lexical branches extend to concealed rancour, inclination or yearning, crookedness and resistant behavior, and holding or wrapping something close to the body. The Quranic noun represents the branch of inward hostility.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized singular citation form ضِغْنٌ; the supplied QAC group attests its plural أَضْغَانَ in two Quran occurrences.

senses.definition: Deep rancour, malice, enmity, or hatred held in the heart.
senses.usage_conditions: Quranically attested in the plural أَضْغَانَ, including hostility concealed or held inwardly; the attached pronouns vary by context.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be or become affected with rancour, malice, spite, or enmity.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Said of a person or of the bosom as the seat of such feelings.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To incline or lean toward someone, against someone, or toward worldly things.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The direction of inclination is expressed by the accompanying preposition.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To feel desire, yearning, or longing of the soul.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A distinct affective use from rancour and physical inclination.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Mutual rancour, malice, spite, or enmity.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Describes reciprocal hostile feeling held by two or more parties.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To conceive or conceal rancour, malice, or spite against someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The hostile feeling is represented as being kept within the heart.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To take or carry a thing, weapon, or child beneath the armpit or in the bosom.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used for holding an object close against the side or carrying a child in the bosom.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The wrapping or tucking of a garment around the body.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Specifically, a manner of putting part of the garment beneath the arms and drawing it together.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Difficulty of disposition in a beast.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional description of an animal that is difficult or troublesome in temperament.
A nominal expression for personal leaning or attachment.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Desire, yearning, or longing of the soul.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: May describe an animal's pull toward its accustomed home and companions, and may be used metaphorically of women.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A side, region, quarter, or tract; specifically, the foot or lowest part of a mountain.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The mountain sense denotes its lower side or base.
An adjectival description of one affected by hostile feeling.
Used tropically of a crooked spear-shaft.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A horse or mare that runs by reverting from the state or course it had been following.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An equine term describing a return or deviation from the prior running state or course.
A designation explained by association with rancour or fierceness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A horse that does not exert its full running power unless beaten.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An equine description of reluctance to run at full strength.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who treats or regards another, especially a brother, with rancour, malice, spite, or enmity.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression can imply reciprocal hostile treatment between the parties.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Pointer-only unit directing the reader to the following material.
Holding or carrying beneath the bosom or side.
Rancour and violent hatred; its plural is the Quranic أَضْغَانَ.
Difficulty of disposition in a beast.
Foot or lowest part of a mountain.

cautions: The Quranic form is attested only as the inflected plural أَضْغَانَ; the public headword is normalized to the singular citation form ضِغْنٌ.
The Form VIII classical headword is normalized as اِضْطَغَنَ; the Lane heading records the orthographic variant إِضْتَغَنَ while its lexical examples use اضطغن.
